headline.text: The FDA calcitriol label names additive effects and hypercalcemia with pharmacological doses of vitamin D.

reported.text: The FDA calcitriol label calls calcitriol the most potent active metabolite of vitamin D3 and says additive effects and hypercalcemia are possible with pharmacological vitamin D doses.

claims.text: The FDA calcitriol label says pharmacological doses of vitamin D and its derivatives are to be withheld during calcitriol treatment because of possible additive effects and hypercalcemia.
claims.quote: Since calcitriol is the most potent active metabolite of vitamin D 3 , pharmacological doses of vitamin D and its derivatives should be withheld during treatment with calcitriol to avoid possible additive effects and hypercalcemia (see WARNINGS ).
claims.judgeRationale: The calcitriol label says pharmacological doses of vitamin D (which includes cholecalciferol) should be withheld to avoid additive effects and hypercalcemia.

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines contain Calcitriol or Cholecalciferol, or work the same way?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Calcitriol and Cholecalciferol, change how much this matters?
